subject: Using Shiny widgets to control Javascript?

messages.author: aacdf4534922e52f
messages.subject: Using Shiny widgets to control Javascript?
parts:
I'm working with rgl's WebGL output, and I'd like to use Shiny widgets to control the display.  Because rgl writes out so much code for each scene, the display is quite sluggish in response to changes requested by the user via widgets.  I'm looking into different approaches to fix this.

The simplest approach might be to work entirely in Javascript within the user's browser.  I would write some Javascript code that gets called when the widget is changed, and it tells the rest of the WebGL code what to do.  The reason I want to involve Shiny here is that I'd like some widgets to work this way, while others will need to talk to the server to do some more extensive computing.  I want all the widgets to look the same.

A more complicated approach could be to make custom widgets that just change part of the web page, without requiring the whole thing to be replaced.  I think this is the way the more extensive changes should be done, but there will be a delay for the round-trip to the server even if not much is being sent.

The goal is to make responses to Shiny widgets as quick as purely local changes, e.g. scene rotation.  Are there examples like this out there?
